title: Platelets thirty-one thousand
objective: Screen before testing: avoid studies over open skin infection, burns, recent grafts or casts; defer or limit needle EMG with platelets below 50,000; treat lymphedema as no contraindication to needle EMG, weighing the risk against what the study adds; and avoid testing with external temporary pacemakers
secondaryObjectives: Lower bleeding risk in needle EMG for patients on anticoagulants or with bleeding tendencies: use the smallest-gauge needle, limit needle insertions, and skip deep muscles that can't be compressed or that lie near large vessels

brief.situation: 10:00 in an electrodiagnostic laboratory. You are the physical therapist performing a referred right upper limb EMG and nerve conduction study for Mrs. Okafor, 58, with hand numbness. She is on chemotherapy for lymphoma.
handover: The referral asks to 'rule out carpal tunnel versus chemotherapy neuropathy'.
Laboratory policy: review labs, anticoagulants and skin before any needle study; a contraindication is discussed with the referring physician before testing.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: Platelets of 31,000 are below 50,000, so needle EMG is deferred or limited; her lymphedema is not a contraindication; surface nerve conductions carry no bleeding risk.
parts.modelAnswer: Her platelets are 31,000, under the 50,000 line, so no full needle study today. The lymphedema isn't the issue, and surface conductions are fine.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Defers needling, runs the surface studies, calls the oncologist about a limited study after recovery using the smallest needle, few insertions and no deep non-compressible muscles.
parts.modelAnswer: Defer the needle part, do the conductions, and call the oncologist. If we needle later, smallest needle, few insertions, nothing deep.
